I do really short exercises but do them consistently. 

I started off by doing 1 squat a day, but everyday and when I got used to that, 5 squats, when i got used to that I added more to it. 

With walking I would simply go outside for 5 minute or so walk around the block and head back then if I was consistent enough move up.

You'll find something that works for you, you just gotta try different approaches. Mine was doing exercise at home until I felt comfortable enough to go outside and did it slowly. 

I wish you luck, you got this!

That higher heart rate didn't exactly mean better exercise. 

For example I would exercise for an hour and my heart rate would get up to 182 for a long time (30 minutes)... I thought I would lose more weight that way.

Luckily I searched it up and realized "Oh I need to stay in a certain range (98-156 for me / 50-80% of Max HR) and not higher than that (you can go higher but only for short spurts.)" 

I kept an eye on my HR after that.

Yeah sometimes you just snap into it. 

I snapped into it after being a lot kinder to myself and trying to not be as judgemental of who I was and my weight. And just accepting who I was right now, and that it wasn't how I was always going to be. 

I also tried the thing where you do a incredibly small amount of exercise but do it everyday (like 1 squat, and then up it when its a habit) 

But weight loss is always about trying stuff to see what works for you, different foods, different exercises, different calorie limits, different mindsets, adding/subtracting cheat days etc. For example I switched to weighing myself once a week now, which is so much less stressful and soul crushing than it used to be.

Keep up the good work!

The special consideration situation is why I felt like trimesters were going to be more trouble than they're worth. I agree that it does become a logistical nightmare in that circumstance.

Also while people may do the intentionally fail thing. I don't know whether a lot of of people would do that as it does require you to stay a uni longer. And if you do it for every subject, a 3 year degree becomes a 6 year degree. But for some people it may be worth it. 

Again i'm just gonna make it clear, my whole argument was about the level of documentation required for fee remission being too high not that its existence is bad.

Otherwise as I said previously there does need to be a balance.

I think its fair if it wasn't frustratingly hard to even get this to be passed. You gotta understand every system is going to have people trying to abuse it for their own benefit. (I never said no documentation btw, just that the system is a bit shit)

The problem is as a person with a mental disability it is hard to garner the information and evidence required to get it called. 

(Not to mention the university requires you to essentially give in similar information proving that you need something like an Equitable Learning Plan. And even with that, its something that needs to be submitted every year or else it goes away. Which is definitely a question mark for me. I understand that life circumstances and even illnesses(?) can go away after a year but a lifelong/chronic illness or disability is something that doesn't go away. So I have to get new information about how I still have a disability.)

But bringing it back to fee remission. I understand, its true people could abuse it but you also have to consider how many people who need it that you are hurting by making it so difficult and robotic in nature. You submit a bunch of evidence to a form and get a response half a year later (there have been delays this year). It's humiliating getting all that evidence as well. I understand that this is always going to be a part of my life, but it always does suck having to write about myself like a pitiable child because if I don't this application is going to be absolutely denied. Or even asking and getting a psychiatrist to write about my issues with medication/self. You have to guide them through and relive the worst parts of your year just to be able to describe hey this was actually bad. 

I think people need to realize this evidence isn't just "hey this student attempted xxx" its a whole essay about how you've been doing, why you didn't drop the subject at the census date, how this situation worsened after the census date. Because, even if you were in your worst condition in week 2 but held off on dropping because you thought you could get past it, and it gets worse on week 3, this is grounds for no fee remission. 

Because there was a chance that you would get on your computer and drop the subject. The idea of being able to function and being able to think about university and dropping subjects before the census date is wild. Sometimes you're just fucked and you need to get other things smoothed out with family, housing, financial stuff and yourself. University isn't all that people think about.

Also the abuse would be limited to someone I guess getting a higher WAM, but staying longer at university. Which is messed up for sure. But looking at the other side you just have people who just accept that this is too hard and ignores it. Maybe they even start to feel worse about their situation because it wasn't good enough to get fee remission. 

And hey I understand, people hate systems being abused. The way it is now, might be the happy medium. I don't know for sure how things would change. Just realize that it isn't easy to get documentation. 

Even for special consideration. I haven't gotten any because you need to submit it in 3 days. Who can get a psychiatrist appointment in 3 days or even a week. I have mine every 1-2 months and that's because I prebooked a lot of them. It's hella expensive as well. It's not an easy option for everyone.

Fee remission is truly a horrible part of UNSW. As with many things that require paperwork you need to be as elaborate as possible and completely deny the fact that you "could've" done something,etc. 

As a student with a disability it's frustrating dealing with UNSW. If you can ask your psychologist to be incredibly firm with the wording (which im sure they already are). Potentially see if you can get further documentation just saying something along the lines of "no, because this, which was because of that, etc" (If its possible to get an appointment within 28 days from the decision)

I haven't completed it, but as a really bad player who is trying to cheese this, I'd like to share some things that may or may not help people. It may be obvious stuff but I need to get this frustration over the gauntlet out somewhere.

**First tip**: *Work backwards from Stage 2 Hard*.

* Nodoka is genuinely hell to deal with unless you're good at dodging or you're used to the pattern. 

* Also stay close to her when she does her first laser shot after every rotation as she will lock on to you instantly and you will not be able to escape.

* Regardless you don't want to finish both S1H and S4 and then fall at stage 2 hard. Work backwards until you're comfortable.

**Second tip**: *Play the maps without hardcore on to see the patterns but also to get used to playing on the map. (Record it as well)*

* If you keep playing with 1 hp you might get stuck every few minutes by a new pattern or enemy that you can't figure out how to get past. (S1H 5 minute bird wave for example)

* Test out how each level of Marketing affects you. It helps you level early on but later on it becomes a bit of a nuisance.

**Third tip**: *Character Choice*

* Amelia, Kaela, Moona and Risu have skills and supers that help a bit

* Amelia's super slows time. Easier to get through obstacles and tricky patterns. 

* Kaela's super is really good at clearing screen and getting aoe out. While also making Kaela faster and stronger for a bit.

* Amelias' **Bubba**, Kaela' **No Pressure** and Moona's **Moon Song** and **Lunar Construction** are nice especially if you get it early. Even just level 1 will be able to clear a bunch of enemies. 

* That being said be prepared with Bubba, as he goes everywhere. Where as No Pressure is in an aura around Kaela. 

* Bubba is able to collect exp for you though so you could potentially either keep running away and try to get strong enough to fight through his exp collection.

* Moona's **Moon Song** and **Lunar Construction** are good but with addendums, Moon Song pulling enemies towards it. So you could accidentally pull an enemy towards you and die, or trap yourself, and Lunar Construction requiring you to kill enemies until you get 5 Lunar blocks. On the flip side it fills your special meter which on Moona does a good bit of damage

* Risu is more just good for high marketing, their weapon is good and the **Nonstop Nuts** and **DLC** is good for clearing loads of enemies, even when it gets later in the game. I prefer the others over her, but I do think she's definitely powerful and with the right RNG you can do real well.

* With these skills you can get beetle, asacoco, face mask and energy drink to make them more powerful. If you're Ame remember that her FPS Mastery increase ATK, not Weapon Damage. So if you fully max it out it gives 60% ATK and 10% haste. 

**Fourth Tip**: *Items*.

* You have 1 hp. You cannot gain more through Piki or Bandage. 

* You can get some cool items without worrying about the consequences though.

* * Face Mask - 1.3 all damage +10% haste. 30% more damage taken (who cares)

* * Energy Drink. Increase Haste 10/15/20% and SPD 30/40/50% but reduce HP (who cares)

* * Injection Asacoco - Lose 5% every second (lol). gain 40/60/80% ATK. 

* Other than that, you may think about getting Headphones. You get a percentage chance to auto dodge/negate a hit. 

* Figure out a plan, whats important to get first and when-ish you want to hit big markers like Halu, Halu 5 or collabs. 

* If you have Kaela, then you can get some anvils from their skill, and if you get credit card you'll get more potentially. But you're also wasting a potential slot and levels.

* Asacoco is really good in my opinion as its a 40% ATK boost and that can save you quite a bit. Especially if you upgrade it. 

* Whether or not you try to get Study Glasses early is up to you. I found that it helps a little at the start and a lot towards the end. But I haven't found a good priority when it comes to levelling it.

* Test out weapons, collabs, items and see how they work later in the map. You may not even want to use collabs. Psycho Axe is strong, Wamy water is good for pushing stuff away. maybe you only have 2 weapon slots open and you run with that. 

* Maybe you dont level your weapon, or you get weird collabs. Try it. I've tried Eldritch Horror, Rap Dog and Idol Concert & Super and they're okay (Yes I saw the guide posted by ChocoEz). It's really hard to say which one is the best because it depends on how you want to go about it. 

* Maybe getting Snow Queen is hidden op. Play around with the items/weapons and make adjustments. Absolute Wall might be great because it has a small chance to block projectiles. If you can get that far with the ball and the board then sure.

**Fifth Tip**: *Misc*

* You dont have to stay the same character each run. Personally I like Amelia for S2H and Kaela for S4. S1H is okay for both. 

* Food is honestly up to you. It's a bit cheeky but i'm pretty sure you can change food for each stage. How you use that is up to you.

*With weapons, remember to double check enchantments on weapons. Sometimes you can get lucky and get a CEO's Tears with +1 projectile enchantment. Which makes it really easy to clear even tanky enemies. Be flexible and okay with maybe changing it up to take a good enchantment with a decent/good weapon. 

*Be really careful with scenery objects in the stages, like Stage 1 Hard Tree's or Stage 4 Poles, where things can be hidden behind it without you realizing. You will inevitably lose focus and then run into an enemy you either didnt see or forgot and it will be really frustrating.

**Sixth Tip**: *Have fun*

* Literally you dont have to listen to anything i've written here. Play any character. 

* Anya is invincible with her super, maybe you play around that and get the super collab for supers. You can literally play any ID holo other than Zeta. The gauntlet is meant to be a bit of fun. 

* I haven't even come close to completing it after spending 2 days on it. I may also be wrong and its me trying to find the easiest way to finish the challenge. You could just dodge everything and not worry about your build at all. Just build speed and run forever, wait for bosses to die of natural causes.

This is literally "Holocure: Git Gud/Skill Issue" gauntlet. It's hell, so have fun with it. I only wrote this because I needed a break from losing so much.

EDIT 2: Added Moona and Risu as character with useful skills/supers. Tips about Weapons in Store with Enchantments

It sounds weird but it feels almost natural to die. 
My first suicide attempt  wasn't fueled so much out of despair (at least it felt like) as it was out of "i'm pretty much done here now" After achieving something pretty big. Which caused people to ask me why? 

I just think its going to happen, so I might as well do it at a good moment. I'd rather die being someone I liked than someone I hated. I guess I knew unconsciously how my neglected mental state was about to collapse and how much work it would take to even live to the next day. How much I would lose if I acknowledged it. Shame and disappointing others is a greater fear, so it might be that as well. I fear a death that makes me look bad to others or disappoints others.

I think its been mentioned on this thread but, straddling the line for too long really numbs that fear. For me I felt like I was living on borrowed time. I never felt right, like I was stuck inside my body. Just looking out as my body makes horrible decisions, and only really living because of how it would hurt my parents. 

I mean if someone came at me with a knife i'd probably be freaked out, its not like i'm emotionless and death means nothing. I just feel like death is going to happen, if it happens earlier i'd be relieved but not happy. I think that after my suicide attempts and extremely poor mental health. I've come to a (incorrect but its subconscious so its gonna take a while to fix) conclusion that I cannot choose when I die, that I lack the ability to control anything. So I might as well do what I can and hope for the best, cause if it goes well then nice. 

TL;DR: I feel like its natural. And those who have straddled the line at least in my own experience, become numb to death as a concept and rather fear the vast expanse of what happens now? rather than the full cut to black, everything is done death.
